newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Nov industrial output rose 0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nov industrial output rose 0.9 pct.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board report of U.S. industrial production and capacity utilization, seasonally adjusted.

Wall Street economists expected November industrial production to rise 0.6 percent from October and estimated that November capacity use would be at a rate of 83.0 percent.
The jump in November industrial output was the strongest in nine months, since a 1.3 percent increase last February.

The Fed said about half the November increase was due to a rebound in production of motor vehicles at strike-afffected General Motors plants as well as parts for them. In addition, unusually cold weather boosted utilities output strongly, the Fed said, adding about 0.2 percent to the November growth in industrial output.
Motor vehicle assemblies rose in November to a rate of 6.3 million a year for cars from 5.5 million in October. For light trucks the assembly rate was up to 5.6 million from 5.4 million.
Excluding motor vehicles and parts, November industrial output rose 0.6 percent after rising 0.2 percent in October.
